title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 141
paragraphs: So Alexander spoke. The Lacedaemonians, having been told that Alexander had come to Athens to bring the Athenians to a treaty with the barbarians, and remembering the oracles — which said that it was destined for them, together with the other Dorians, to be driven out of the Peloponnese by the Medes and the Athenians combined — had become very afraid that the Athenians would indeed make a treaty with the Persians, and had resolved at once to send envoys. It so happened that they were introduced at the same time as Alexander; for the Athenians had delayed matters, well aware that the Lacedaemonians would hear that an envoy had come from the barbarians to make a treaty and, hearing this, would send envoys themselves with all speed. So the Athenians acted deliberately to let the Lacedaemonians see their inclination.
